text:
tom: follow-up from the CP separation RFC — spike idea: use short-lived regional anchors but ship an "offline bundle" workflow for air-gapped/private installs. want quick feedback on edge cases.
mei: love the idea. two immediate Qs: how do we revoke a bundle mid-rotation, and how do we minimize cert churn for streaming sessions?
andre: revoke = include a revocation-list endpoint or bump the bundle serial and force a short grace window. streaming: use session tokens separate from certs so streams can resume while certs rotate underneath.
cassie: session tokens need to be revocable too. propose a token format with anchor_id, issued_at, expiry and a revocation nonce checked at handshake.
mei: agreed. also need a practical ops path for customers: a CLI to generate/upload bundles, and a UI in Console to show active bundle serials. docs must warn about clock skew.
tom: good points. sketch of offline bundle CLI:
```
redwoodctl bundle create --region us-west-2 --ttl 4h --out bundle-usw2.tar.gz
# customer uploads bundle to private controlplane
```
kevin: for hosted, prefer dynamic signer + short-lived leaf certs. offline bundle only for Private. bundle contents: leaf cert, anchor_id, serial, valid_from, valid_until, optional CRL. Keep bundle size small.
andre: discovery: clients should try (1) explicit env override, (2) local bundle socket/file, (3) SRV (hosted), (4) global fallback. default timeouts: 40ms, 70ms, 200ms, 800ms.
ops-bot: perf-spike scheduled: SRV vs local-registry next Wed 03:30 UTC
cassie: cache warmup: add a prewarm API and a prioritized hot-list. prewarm call example: POST /v1/prefetch {"prefixes":["/embed/vec","/cache/pfx123"]} returns 202 + progress stream. keep auth tight.
mei: bandwidth cost estimate: top-100 prefixes ~= 15-40MB depending on model. we should make prewarm opt-in for Private to avoid cross-cust billing surprises.
andre: handoff semantics: anchor signals DRAIN_START, clients get 2x write window where writes are mirrored to both anchors for X seconds. after DRAIN_COMPLETE, new anchor is authoritative. ops must be able to force-cutover with a documented risk.
tom: add health endpoint semantics for draining: GET /health?drain=true returns 200 while connections > threshold, 503 when safe to remove. LB automation will respect this.
kevin: add metrics/tracing: anchor_id tag on all requests, metric names: cp.handoff.duration, cp.bundle.uploads, cp.stream.resume.success. also log bundle_serial in trace root.
cassie: SDK changes: expose config block with discovery order + timeouts and a flag enable_offline_bundle=true. example config:
```
controlplane:
  discovery_order: [env, local_bundle, srv, global]
  timeouts_ms: [40,70,200,800]
  enable_offline_bundle: true
```
mei: security: bundles signed by global signer or customer keypair? prefer global signer with HSM-protected keys, but allow customer-signed bundles for air-gapped installs with explicit risk acceptance. document this prominently.
andre: plan: 1) security writeup for bundle lifecycle (mei + kevin), 2) SDK patch for discovery + session tokens (cassie + andre), 3) ops CLI + Console hooks (tom + infra), 4) perf spike + bandwidth numbers (ops + mei).
tom: leaving thread open for RFC follow-up. thanks. :thumbsup:
